-- ── This window's own constants (ref-PaperDollFrame.lua:1-4, Benilla-prefixed) ──────────── BENILLA_NUM_STATS = 5 -- NUM_STATS BENILLA_NUM_RESISTANCE_TYPES = 5 -- NUM_RESISTANCE_TYPES ATTACK_POWER_MAGIC_NUMBER = 14 -- ATTACK_POWER_MAGIC_NUMBER -- MagicResFrame1..5's ref `id=` attrs (ref-PaperDollFrame.xml:654-759) — arcane/fire/nature/ -- frost/shadow; Holy(1) never rides the paper doll (only 5 of the 6 schools show here). BENILLA_MAGICRES_IDS = { 6, 2, 3, 4, 5 } -- The window's pages, named exactly as the reference names them -- ("PaperDollFrame"/"PetPaperDollFrame"/"ReputationFrame"/"SkillFrame"/"HonorFrame"). 1:1 -- with the tab row below (index N is tab N's page) — decision 0437 phase 4 added the Skills -- page, decision 1057 the Pet one, ReputationFrame.xml took the real client's own slot 3 -- (which put Skills at the real client's own 4), and HonorFrame.xml takes the 5. -- THE ROSTER IS NOW THE REFERENCE'S, WHOLE: five pages, five tabs, no omission left and -- nothing past the end. The 0138 merchant-tab precedent ("tabs arrive with their pages") is -- what kept this list a prefix of the real one until now, rather than a row of dead tabs. -- `character_tests.rs` pins each page's `id=` against its slot here, which is what kept the -- two in step as the middle of the row filled in. BENILLA_CHARACTERFRAME_SUBFRAMES = { "PaperDollFrame", "PetPaperDollFrame", "ReputationFrame", "SkillFrame", "HonorFrame", }
-- ── The window: toggle / tab dispatch (ref CharacterFrame.lua:1-48) ───────────────────── -- Kept BARE (not Benilla-prefixed) — the addon-facing entry point, matching this codebase's -- own ToggleQuestLog() precedent (QuestLogFrame.xml). function CharacterFrame_ShowSubFrame(frameName) for _, value in ipairs(BENILLA_CHARACTERFRAME_SUBFRAMES) do -- Nil-guarded: a page's file may not be loaded (a test subset, a later -- load-on-demand page) — a missing sibling must never break the switch. local page = getglobal(value) if page then if value == frameName then page:Show() else page:Hide() end end end end
function ToggleCharacter(tab) local subFrame = getglobal(tab) if not subFrame then return end -- ref CharacterFrame.lua:4-6, the pet guard: asking for the pet page with no pet does -- NOTHING — not even close an open window. The `not IsVisible()` half is what still -- lets the page CLOSE itself when the pet vanishes underneath it (the pet page's own -- OnEvent calls straight back in here to do exactly that). Hoisted below the getglobal -- (the ref tests it above) purely so the visibility read has a frame to ask. if tab == "PetPaperDollFrame" and not HasPetUI() and not subFrame:IsVisible() then return end local frame = getglobal("CharacterFrame") -- ref CharacterFrame.lua:11, and the line whose absence desynced this window: the tab -- row is selected HERE, from the page's own id, on EVERY path — including the one that -- closes the window. Having it only on the tab-button OnClick meant a KEYBIND -- (`C`/`SHIFT-P`, which call straight in here) switched the page and left the row -- selecting the old tab; clicking that old tab then took the "already visible" branch -- and shut the window instead of switching back (director, 2026-08-06). The id is the -- page's own `id=` attribute — the loader really does apply it (loader/geometry.rs -- SetID) — and `character_tests.rs` pins every page's id against its slot in -- BENILLA_CHARACTERFRAME_SUBFRAMES, which is what keeps the two in step the day -- Reputation lands between them. PanelTemplates_SetTab(frame, subFrame:GetID()) if frame:IsVisible() then if subFrame:IsVisible() then HideUIPanel(frame) else PlaySound("igCharacterInfoTab") CharacterFrame_ShowSubFrame(tab) end else ShowUIPanel(frame) CharacterFrame_ShowSubFrame(tab) end end
-- The tab row's own OnClick (ref CharacterFrameTab_OnClick, l.35-48), now id-based (decision -- 0437 phase 4 grows the row to 2) — the MerchantFrame.xml Merchant/Buyback pair's own shape -- for a >1-tab window: `id` indexes BOTH the tab button and BENILLA_CHARACTERFRAME_SUBFRAMES -- 1:1. It does NOT select the tab itself — the ref's own tab OnClick doesn't either, because -- ToggleCharacter is the single place that does it (above), so the click path and the -- keybind path cannot disagree. l.47's trailing PlaySound is the ref's OWN redundant second -- igCharacterInfoTab — ToggleCharacter already plays it on the "switch to this tab" path, so -- this second call only matters when the window is ALREADY open on this same tab, i.e. the -- HideUIPanel branch — kept rather than "fixed" since it's the ref's own -- behavior, not a bug of ours. function BenillaCharacterFrameTab_OnClick(id) ToggleCharacter(BENILLA_CHARACTERFRAME_SUBFRAMES[id]) PlaySound("igCharacterInfoTab") end
function CharacterFrame_OnLoad() local frame = this -- GetID()/SetID() DO exist (landed with slice 2's BagFrame, which relies on them for -- its own per-window bag id) — the STALE claim this comment used to make is corrected -- here (0208 phase 1b touched this function anyway). All 5 tabs ship with the Honor -- page (Character + Pet + Reputation + Skills + Honor — the reference's own five); the -- window opens on tab 1 by default, matching the real client. Tab 2 raises and hides -- itself with the pet — PetTab_Update, which the pet page runs at its own OnLoad and on -- every pet transition — so the COUNT here is the full row, not the currently-visible -- one, which is why this number reaches the ref's own SetNumTabs(5) rather than -- tracking what is on screen. PanelTemplates_SetNumTabs(frame, 5) PanelTemplates_SetTab(frame, 1) -- The reference LABELS its numerals here (CharacterFrame_OnLoad l.55-57: "Health" on -- the player's health bar, "XP" on the XP bar, with the power bar's following the -- resource in UnitFrames.xml). Shipped in 1146 and cut the same day on the director's -- call — bare numbers read better on our bars (decision 1147). The mechanism is -- untouched and live: SetTextStatusBarTextPrefix works, and restoring any one of the -- three is the one line the reference has. If it is ever restored, note the ordering -- it depends on — a prefix only sticks on a bar that already has its TextString, and -- this file's seat works only because the manifest runs UnitFrames (52) and ActionBar -- (76) well ahead of it (149), exactly as FrameXML runs PlayerFrame (44) and -- MainMenuBar (34) ahead of CharacterFrame (53). end
-- ref CharacterFrame_OnShow (l.82-93). The Show*TextStatusBarText calls are LIVE as of -- decision 1146 — the note that used to sit here ("no unit-frame bar-text-mode toggle -- exists in this engine") was true when it was written and stopped being true when the -- numerals landed (1143). Opening the character sheet reveals your own and your pet's -- numbers for as long as it is open, whatever Status Bar Text says, through the same -- lockShow refcount the hover uses — so a hover inside an open sheet still balances. -- ShowWatchedReputationBarText is LIVE too, since the Reputation tab landed and with it a -- driven watch bar (ActionBar.xml owns both, its own placement note says why): opening the -- sheet reveals the watched faction's numbers for as long as it is open, exactly like the -- five bars above. Guarded on existence like its neighbours — the engine's per-window -- harnesses load this file without ActionBar.xml. -- UnitPVPName -> plain UnitName (this file's header comment: PVP rank is a named deferral). function CharacterFrame_OnShow() if UpdateMicroButtons then UpdateMicroButtons() end PlaySound("igCharacterInfoOpen") SetPortraitTexture(getglobal("CharacterFramePortrait"), "player") getglobal("CharacterNameText"):SetText(UnitName("player")) if ShowTextStatusBarText then -- engine tests load file subsets ShowTextStatusBarText(PlayerFrameHealthBar) ShowTextStatusBarText(PlayerFramePowerBar) ShowTextStatusBarText(MainMenuExpBar) ShowTextStatusBarText(PetFrameHealthBar) ShowTextStatusBarText(PetFrameManaBar) end if ShowWatchedReputationBarText then ShowWatchedReputationBarText() end end
-- ref CharacterFrame_OnHide (l.95-104): everything past the PlaySound is the OnShow list's -- Hide-twin — UpdateMicroButtons live (MicroMenu.xml), the bar-text calls live too (1146), -- and the reputation one live since the watch bar started being driven. The subframe hide-loop is OUR OWN addition -- (decision 0437 phase 4): PaperDollFrame is a true engine child of this frame (its -- own header comment) so it hides for free on the parent's Hide-cascade, but -- SkillFrame is a SEPARATE top-level file — this engine has no cross-file `parent=` -- attachment (grepped `benilla-ui/src/loader`: the XML `parent=` attribute is read nowhere, -- unlike `relativeTo`, which resolves by name regardless of tree position — see -- SkillFrame.xml's own header comment) — so nothing else would hide it when the WHOLE -- character window closes (ESC, the close X, or another left-slot window bumping it via -- UIPanel exclusivity). Looping every BENILLA_CHARACTERFRAME_SUBFRAMES entry here, once, is -- what carried that correctness through every non-nested tab that followed — Pet, -- Reputation and now Honor, all four of the five pages that are separate files. function CharacterFrame_OnHide() if UpdateMicroButtons then UpdateMicroButtons() end PlaySound("igCharacterInfoClose") if HideTextStatusBarText then -- engine tests load file subsets HideTextStatusBarText(PlayerFrameHealthBar) HideTextStatusBarText(PlayerFramePowerBar) HideTextStatusBarText(MainMenuExpBar) HideTextStatusBarText(PetFrameHealthBar) HideTextStatusBarText(PetFrameManaBar) end if HideWatchedReputationBarText then HideWatchedReputationBarText() end for _, name in ipairs(BENILLA_CHARACTERFRAME_SUBFRAMES) do local subFrame = getglobal(name) if subFrame then subFrame:Hide() end end end
-- ── The paper-doll page (ref PaperDollFrame.lua) ──────────────────────────────────────── -- ref PaperDollFrame_OnLoad (l.6-29), the label lines (l.7-13) kept as the ref has them: the -- labels live ONLY in the row template's $parentLabel (gold GameFontNormalSmall, LEFT) and -- Lua fills them — never a re-declared region in an instance (the ref's instances carry no -- <Layers> at all, and this engine's template expansion appends children, so a re-declared -- $parentLabel creates a SECOND anchorless default-font FontString instead of merging — the -- white/overlapping-label bug this line-set replaces). CHARACTER_POINTS_CHANGED/ -- UNIT_MODEL_CHANGED/PLAYER_DAMAGE_DONE_MODS/UNIT_RANGEDDAMAGE/PLAYER_GUILD_UPDATE/ -- SKILL_LINES_CHANGED are OMITTED (talents/guild/skills are out of this phase's event -- contract; UNIT_RANGEDDAMAGE isn't in it either — UNIT_DAMAGE/UNIT_ATTACK_SPEED alone -- trigger the ranged refresh below, same as the ref's own first branch already does). function PaperDollFrame_OnLoad() local frame = this getglobal("CharacterAttackFrameLabel"):SetText(MELEE_ATTACK) getglobal("CharacterDamageFrameLabel"):SetText(DAMAGE_COLON) getglobal("CharacterAttackPowerFrameLabel"):SetText(ATTACK_POWER_COLON) getglobal("CharacterRangedAttackFrameLabel"):SetText(RANGED_ATTACK) getglobal("CharacterRangedDamageFrameLabel"):SetText(DAMAGE_COLON) getglobal("CharacterRangedAttackPowerFrameLabel"):SetText(ATTACK_POWER_COLON) getglobal("CharacterArmorFrameLabel"):SetText(ARMOR_COLON) frame:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_LEVEL") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_RESISTANCES") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_STATS") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_DAMAGE") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_ATTACK_SPEED") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_ATTACK_POWER") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_RANGED_ATTACK_POWER") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_ATTACK") end
-- Every row of the sheet, in the order a full repaint fills them. The order is load-bearing -- at the ranged end: SetRangedAttack is what decides `PaperDollFrame.noRanged`, and the two -- ranged rows after it read that flag rather than re-deciding it. -- -- Rows are NAMED, not referenced. Resolving each through the global table at call time is -- what the reference's own call-by-name got for free, and the paper-doll setters are prime -- addon-hook territory: a table of captured function values would keep calling the setter an -- addon replaced. local paperDollRows = { "PaperDollFrame_SetLevel", "PaperDollFrame_SetStats", "PaperDollFrame_SetResistances", "PaperDollFrame_SetArmor", "PaperDollFrame_SetDamage", "PaperDollFrame_SetAttackPower", "PaperDollFrame_SetAttackBothHands", "PaperDollFrame_SetRangedAttack", "PaperDollFrame_SetRangedDamage", "PaperDollFrame_SetRangedAttackPower", }
-- A weapon that changed how hard it hits and one that changed how often move the same four -- rows, so the two events share a list rather than a copy of one. local weaponRows = { "PaperDollFrame_SetDamage", "PaperDollFrame_SetRangedAttack", "PaperDollFrame_SetRangedDamage", "PaperDollFrame_SetAttackBothHands", }
-- Which rows a single change moves, keyed by the event reporting it. The reference spells -- this out as an if/elseif ladder and then keeps a second, hand-parallel copy of the row -- order in OnShow; one table read two ways cannot drift the way two call lists do. -- -- Only this file's registered subset appears (see PaperDollFrame_OnLoad's note on the -- omitted events). PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD is registered and deliberately absent: the ref's -- one use for it is `CharacterModelFrame:SetUnit("player")`, and our CharacterModelFrame is -- a booth-texture stand-in rather than a live model widget (this file's header) — there is -- no SetUnit to call. It keeps its early return below rather than a row here, because the -- reference returns on it before even the visibility check. local rowsMovedBy = { UNIT_LEVEL = { "PaperDollFrame_SetLevel" }, UNIT_STATS = { "PaperDollFrame_SetStats" }, UNIT_RESISTANCES = { "PaperDollFrame_SetResistances", "PaperDollFrame_SetArmor" }, UNIT_ATTACK = { "PaperDollFrame_SetAttackBothHands" }, UNIT_ATTACK_POWER = { "PaperDollFrame_SetAttackPower" }, UNIT_DAMAGE = weaponRows, UNIT_ATTACK_SPEED = weaponRows, UNIT_RANGED_ATTACK_POWER = { "PaperDollFrame_SetRangedAttack", "PaperDollFrame_SetRangedAttackPower", }, }
local function paintRows(rows) for i = 1, table.getn(rows) do getglobal(rows[i])() end end
-- `unit` is the DECLARED second parameter, not the `arg1` global: the XML passes `arg1` into -- it exactly as the reference's own does (PaperDollFrame.xml), so an addon calling the 1.12 -- arity is read correctly rather than off a stale global. Only the player's own sheet is -- driven from here (no pet/other-unit reuse in phase 1a), and only while it is on screen — -- a hidden page is repainted wholesale by OnShow when it comes back. function PaperDollFrame_OnEvent(event, unit) if event == "PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD" then return end if not this:IsVisible() then return end if unit ~= "player" then return end local rows = rowsMovedBy[event] if rows then paintRows(rows) end end
-- ref PaperDollFrame_OnShow (l.568-585): SetGuild OMITTED (named deferral, this file's -- header). The relic Hide/Show branch is DROPPED outright — UnitHasRelicSlot is -- vanilla-always-false, so CharacterAmmoSlot simply never has a reason to hide; it ships -- with no hidden="true" at all (see its own Button below). function PaperDollFrame_OnShow() paintRows(paperDollRows) end -- ref PaperDollFrame_OnHide (l.587-592) is entirely commented-out in the ref itself (the -- ShoppingTooltip/compare-tooltip lines, OMIT) — nothing to transcribe, no OnHide wired.
-- UnitRace/UnitClass return nil,nil until the app's first player snapshot lands (unlike the -- real client, whose race/class are synchronous local data, never network-raced) — "?" is a -- harmless placeholder for that one-tick window, not a fidelity change (verified live: an -- unguarded format() errors "string expected, got nil" the instant this fires before the -- first snapshot). function PaperDollFrame_SetLevel() getglobal("CharacterLevelText"):SetText( format(PLAYER_LEVEL, UnitLevel("player"), UnitRace("player") or "?", UnitClass("player") or "?")) end
-- ref PaperDollFrame_SetStats (l.131-174), including its per-refresh label SetText (l.140) -- — the labels' one source of text (see PaperDollFrame_OnLoad's header comment). function PaperDollFrame_SetStats() for i = 1, BENILLA_NUM_STATS do local label = getglobal("CharacterStatFrame" .. i .. "Label") local text = getglobal("CharacterStatFrame" .. i .. "StatText") local frame = getglobal("CharacterStatFrame" .. i) local statName = getglobal("SPELL_STAT" .. (i - 1) .. "_NAME") label:SetText(statName .. ":") local stat, effectiveStat, posBuff, negBuff = UnitStat("player", i) local tooltipText = HIGHLIGHT_FONT_COLOR_CODE .. statName .. " " if posBuff == 0 and negBuff == 0 then text:SetText(effectiveStat) frame.tooltip = tooltipText .. effectiveStat .. FONT_COLOR_CODE_CLOSE else tooltipText = tooltipText .. effectiveStat if posBuff > 0 or negBuff < 0 then tooltipText = tooltipText .. " (" .. (stat - posBuff - negBuff) .. FONT_COLOR_CODE_CLOSE end if posBuff > 0 then tooltipText = tooltipText .. FONT_COLOR_CODE_CLOSE .. GREEN_FONT_COLOR_CODE .. "+" .. posBuff .. FONT_COLOR_CODE_CLOSE end if negBuff < 0 then tooltipText = tooltipText .. RED_FONT_COLOR_CODE .. " " .. negBuff .. FONT_COLOR_CODE_CLOSE end if posBuff > 0 or negBuff < 0 then tooltipText = tooltipText .. HIGHLIGHT_FONT_COLOR_CODE .. ")" .. FONT_COLOR_CODE_CLOSE end frame.tooltip = tooltipText if negBuff < 0 then text:SetText(RED_FONT_COLOR_CODE .. effectiveStat .. FONT_COLOR_CODE_CLOSE) else text:SetText(GREEN_FONT_COLOR_CODE .. effectiveStat .. FONT_COLOR_CODE_CLOSE) end end end end
-- One word for how well a school is covered, from resistance-per-level. The bands descend, -- so the first threshold cleared names it and a ratio of zero or less clears none of them. -- (The reference leaves the answer in an implicit global; a pure function of the ratio is -- both the honest shape and one less name in our sandboxed globals table.) local function resistanceBand(ratio) if ratio > 5 then return RESISTANCE_EXCELLENT end if ratio > 3.75 then return RESISTANCE_VERYGOOD end if ratio > 2.5 then return RESISTANCE_GOOD end if ratio > 1.25 then return RESISTANCE_FAIR end if ratio > 0 then return RESISTANCE_POOR end return RESISTANCE_NONE end
-- ref PaperDollFrame_SetResistances (l.176-228). function PaperDollFrame_SetResistances() for i = 1, BENILLA_NUM_RESISTANCE_TYPES do local resistId = BENILLA_MAGICRES_IDS[i] local text = getglobal("MagicResText" .. i) local frame = getglobal("MagicResFrame" .. i) local base, resistance, positive, negative = UnitResistance("player", resistId) local resistanceName = getglobal("RESISTANCE" .. resistId .. "_NAME") frame.tooltip = resistanceName .. " " .. resistance if math.abs(negative) > positive then text:SetText(RED_FONT_COLOR_CODE .. resistance .. FONT_COLOR_CODE_CLOSE) elseif math.abs(negative) == positive then text:SetText(resistance) else text:SetText(GREEN_FONT_COLOR_CODE .. resistance .. FONT_COLOR_CODE_CLOSE) end if positive ~= 0 or negative ~= 0 then frame.tooltip = frame.tooltip .. " ( " .. HIGHLIGHT_FONT_COLOR_CODE .. base if positive > 0 then frame.tooltip = frame.tooltip .. GREEN_FONT_COLOR_CODE .. " +" .. positive end if negative < 0 then frame.tooltip = frame.tooltip .. " " .. RED_FONT_COLOR_CODE .. negative end frame.tooltip = frame.tooltip .. FONT_COLOR_CODE_CLOSE .. " )" end -- The divisor floors at 20 because the reference does (l.210-211: it reads the level, -- then clamps on the NEXT line — an earlier note here cited l.210 alone and called -- the floor ours). The `or 1` is the only difference: the ref would error on a nil -- level, and nothing is gained by reproducing that. local unitLevel = math.max(UnitLevel("player") or 1, 20) frame.tooltipSubtext = format(RESISTANCE_TOOLTIP_SUBTEXT, getglobal("RESISTANCE_TYPE" .. resistId), unitLevel, resistanceBand(resistance / unitLevel)) end end
-- ref PaperDollFrame_SetArmor (l.230-250). NOTE the ref's own third UnitArmor return -- (`armor`) is unused here too — PaperDollFormatStat gets `base`, not `armor`; the ref's -- behavior kept, not "fixed". function PaperDollFrame_SetArmor(unit, prefix) unit = unit or "player" prefix = prefix or "Character" local base, effectiveArmor, armor, posBuff, negBuff = UnitArmor(unit) local frame = getglobal(prefix .. "ArmorFrame") local text = getglobal(prefix .. "ArmorFrameStatText") PaperDollFormatStat(ARMOR, base, posBuff, negBuff, frame, text) local playerLevel = UnitLevel(unit) local armorReduction = effectiveArmor / ((85 * playerLevel) + 400) armorReduction = 100 * (armorReduction / (armorReduction + 1)) frame.tooltipSubtext = format(ARMOR_TOOLTIP, playerLevel, armorReduction) end
-- ref PaperDollFrame_SetDefense (l.252-272). Shared like every setter around it, but the -- CHARACTER sheet has no defense row — the real client's doesn't either, and this exists -- solely for the pet page (decision 1057), which is why it arrives now and not in 0208. -- `UnitDefense`'s second return is a single signed modifier, not the pos/neg pair the other -- setters get, so the split into posBuff/negBuff happens here. function PaperDollFrame_SetDefense(unit, prefix) unit = unit or "player" prefix = prefix or "Character" local base, modifier = UnitDefense(unit) local frame = getglobal(prefix .. "DefenseFrame") local text = getglobal(prefix .. "DefenseFrameStatText") -- The sign is all that decides which side of the pair the one modifier lands on, and a -- modifier of zero lands on neither. PaperDollFormatStat(DEFENSE_COLON, base, math.max(modifier, 0), math.min(modifier, 0), frame, text) end
-- ── Weapon swings: the arithmetic and the wording, once ──────────────────────────────────── -- Three rows read a swing — main hand, off hand, ranged — and it is the same calculation -- with the same vocabulary each time, so it lives here instead of two and three times over.
-- The sheet's green and red for damage figures. Byte-identical to Fonts.xml's GREEN/RED -- font-colour codes today, and kept separate on purpose: these are the damage row's own -- colours, and reading them off the font palette would tie one to the other. local DAMAGE_UP_COLOR = "|cff20ff20" local DAMAGE_DOWN_COLOR = "|cffff2020"
-- What the weapon itself swings for. The numbers we are handed already have the flat -- physical bonuses added and the percent multiplier applied; the row shows those, but the -- tooltip breaks out where they came from, so the un-modified swing has to be recovered. -- Returns that raw range, the modified average, and the gap the modifiers make between them. local function unscaleSwing(minDamage, maxDamage, bonusPos, bonusNeg, percent) local rawMin = (minDamage / percent) - bonusPos - bonusNeg local rawMax = (maxDamage / percent) - bonusPos - bonusNeg local baseDamage = (rawMin + rawMax) * 0.5 local fullDamage = (baseDamage + bonusPos + bonusNeg) * percent return rawMin, rawMax, fullDamage, fullDamage - baseDamage end
-- Both ends of a swing, rounded outwards and floored at 1 — a weapon swinging for a -- fraction of a point still reads as a weapon. local function swingBounds(minDamage, maxDamage) return math.max(math.floor(minDamage), 1), math.max(math.ceil(maxDamage), 1) end
-- The range as a tooltip writes it, always spaced. local function damageRange(minDamage, maxDamage) local low, high = swingBounds(minDamage, maxDamage) return low .. " - " .. high end
-- The range as the ROW writes it: spaced while both ends are two digits, tightened up once -- either reaches three and the row starts running out of width. local function damageFigure(minDamage, maxDamage) local low, high = swingBounds(minDamage, maxDamage) if low < 100 and high < 100 then return low .. " - " .. high end return low .. "-" .. high end
-- The tooltip's account of what modified the raw range: the flat bonus, then the multiplier, -- each coloured by which way it went and left out entirely when it is not in play. local function damageModifiers(tooltip, bonusPos, bonusNeg, percent) if bonusPos > 0 then tooltip = tooltip .. DAMAGE_UP_COLOR .. " +" .. bonusPos .. "|r" end if bonusNeg < 0 then tooltip = tooltip .. DAMAGE_DOWN_COLOR .. " " .. bonusNeg .. "|r" end if percent > 1 then tooltip = tooltip .. DAMAGE_UP_COLOR .. " x" .. math.floor(percent * 100 + 0.5) .. "%|r" elseif percent < 1 then tooltip = tooltip .. DAMAGE_DOWN_COLOR .. " x" .. math.floor(percent * 100 + 0.5) .. "%|r" end return tooltip end
-- Which way a modified figure is tinted. Only asked once a caller knows something modified -- it, so a zero bonus never reaches here and has no colour of its own. local function damageColor(totalBonus) if totalBonus > 0 then return DAMAGE_UP_COLOR end return DAMAGE_DOWN_COLOR end
-- ref PaperDollFrame_SetDamage (l.274-372). The off hand is the same swing read twice: the -- flat bonuses and the multiplier are the character's, not the weapon's, so both hands take -- them, and only the speed and the raw range differ. function PaperDollFrame_SetDamage(unit, prefix) unit = unit or "player" prefix = prefix or "Character" local damageText = getglobal(prefix .. "DamageFrameStatText") local damageFrame = getglobal(prefix .. "DamageFrame") local speed, offhandSpeed = UnitAttackSpeed(unit) local minDamage, maxDamage, minOffHandDamage, maxOffHandDamage, physicalBonusPos, physicalBonusNeg, percent = UnitDamage(unit) local figure = damageFigure(minDamage, maxDamage) local rawMin, rawMax, fullDamage, totalBonus = unscaleSwing(minDamage, maxDamage, physicalBonusPos, physicalBonusNeg, percent) local damageTooltip = damageRange(rawMin, rawMax) if totalBonus == 0 then damageText:SetText(figure) else damageText:SetText(damageColor(totalBonus) .. figure .. "|r") damageTooltip = damageModifiers(damageTooltip, physicalBonusPos, physicalBonusNeg, percent) end damageFrame.damage = damageTooltip damageFrame.attackSpeed = speed damageFrame.dps = math.max(fullDamage, 1) / speed if offhandSpeed then local offMin, offMax, offhandFullDamage = unscaleSwing( minOffHandDamage, maxOffHandDamage, physicalBonusPos, physicalBonusNeg, percent) -- The off hand gets its breakdown unconditionally: it has no row of its own to keep -- plain, only the tooltip's second half. damageFrame.offhandDamage = damageModifiers(damageRange(offMin, offMax), physicalBonusPos, physicalBonusNeg, percent) damageFrame.offhandAttackSpeed = offhandSpeed damageFrame.offhandDps = math.max(offhandFullDamage, 1) / offhandSpeed else damageFrame.offhandAttackSpeed = nil end end
-- ref PaperDollFrame_SetAttackPower (l.374-389). function PaperDollFrame_SetAttackPower(unit, prefix) unit = unit or "player" prefix = prefix or "Character" local base, posBuff, negBuff = UnitAttackPower(unit) local frame = getglobal(prefix .. "AttackPowerFrame") local text = getglobal(prefix .. "AttackPowerFrameStatText") PaperDollFormatStat(MELEE_ATTACK_POWER, base, posBuff, negBuff, frame, text) frame.tooltipSubtext = format(MELEE_ATTACK_POWER_TOOLTIP, math.max(base + posBuff + negBuff, 0) / ATTACK_POWER_MAGIC_NUMBER) end
-- An attack rating and whatever is moving it, on one row. Nothing moving it means the bare -- number and no hover plate to explain; otherwise the row carries the modified TOTAL, tinted -- by which way it went, and the plate carries the split that produced it. Both the melee row -- and the ranged row read exactly this way. local function setAttackRating(frame, text, base, modifier) if modifier == 0 then text:SetText(base) frame.tooltip = nil return end local color = RED_FONT_COLOR_CODE local sign = " " if modifier > 0 then color = GREEN_FONT_COLOR_CODE sign = " +" end frame.tooltip = base .. color .. sign .. modifier .. FONT_COLOR_CODE_CLOSE text:SetText(color .. (base + modifier) .. FONT_COLOR_CODE_CLOSE) end
-- ref PaperDollFrame_SetAttackBothHands (l.391-417) — the weapon-skill line (decision 0208's -- own "to confirm": the equipped-weapon subclass -> skill-id table is UnitAttackBothHands's -- own concern, not this file's). function PaperDollFrame_SetAttackBothHands(unit, prefix) unit = unit or "player" prefix = prefix or "Character" local mainHandAttackBase, mainHandAttackMod = UnitAttackBothHands(unit) setAttackRating(getglobal(prefix .. "AttackFrame"), getglobal(prefix .. "AttackFrameStatText"), mainHandAttackBase, mainHandAttackMod) end
-- ref PaperDollFrame_SetRangedAttack (l.419-466). `hasRelic`/UnitHasRelicSlot DROPPED -- outright (this file's header comment: vanilla-always-false, dead code in the ref itself). -- The literal slot id 18 is the ref's OWN hardcoded value (l.435) — quoted verbatim; what -- GetInventoryItemTexture resolves id 18 to is the parallel binding's call, not re-derived -- here. function PaperDollFrame_SetRangedAttack(unit, prefix) if unit == "pet" then return end unit = unit or "player" prefix = prefix or "Character" local frame = getglobal(prefix .. "RangedAttackFrame") local text = getglobal(prefix .. "RangedAttackFrameStatText") local paperDoll = getglobal("PaperDollFrame") local rangedAttackBase, rangedAttackMod = UnitRangedAttack(unit) local rangedTexture = GetInventoryItemTexture("player", 18) local oldValue = paperDoll.noRanged if rangedTexture then paperDoll.noRanged = nil else text:SetText(NOT_APPLICABLE) paperDoll.noRanged = true frame.tooltip = nil end if oldValue ~= paperDoll.noRanged then PaperDollFrame_SetRangedAttackPower() PaperDollFrame_SetRangedDamage() end if not rangedTexture then return end setAttackRating(frame, text, rangedAttackBase, rangedAttackMod) end
-- ref PaperDollFrame_SetRangedDamage (l.468-537). function PaperDollFrame_SetRangedDamage(unit, prefix) if unit == "pet" then return end unit = unit or "player" prefix = prefix or "Character" local damageText = getglobal(prefix .. "RangedDamageFrameStatText") local damageFrame = getglobal(prefix .. "RangedDamageFrame") local paperDoll = getglobal("PaperDollFrame") if paperDoll.noRanged then damageText:SetText(NOT_APPLICABLE) damageFrame.damage = nil return end local rangedAttackSpeed, minDamage, maxDamage, physicalBonusPos, physicalBonusNeg, percent = UnitRangedDamage(unit) local figure = damageFigure(minDamage, maxDamage) local rawMin, rawMax, fullDamage, totalBonus = unscaleSwing(minDamage, maxDamage, physicalBonusPos, physicalBonusNeg, percent) local damagePerSecond = math.max(fullDamage, 1) / rangedAttackSpeed local tooltip = damageRange(rawMin, rawMax) if totalBonus == 0 then damageText:SetText(figure) else damageText:SetText(damageColor(totalBonus) .. figure .. "|r") tooltip = damageModifiers(tooltip, physicalBonusPos, physicalBonusNeg, percent) -- Only the modified case gets a hover plate here: an unmodified bow has nothing to -- explain beyond the figure already on the row. damageFrame.tooltip = tooltip .. " " .. format(DPS_TEMPLATE, damagePerSecond) end damageFrame.attackSpeed = rangedAttackSpeed damageFrame.damage = tooltip damageFrame.dps = damagePerSecond end
-- ref PaperDollFrame_SetRangedAttackPower (l.539-566). function PaperDollFrame_SetRangedAttackPower(unit, prefix) if unit == "pet" then return end unit = unit or "player" prefix = prefix or "Character" local frame = getglobal(prefix .. "RangedAttackPowerFrame") local text = getglobal(prefix .. "RangedAttackPowerFrameStatText") local paperDoll = getglobal("PaperDollFrame") if paperDoll.noRanged then text:SetText(NOT_APPLICABLE) frame.tooltip = nil return end if HasWandEquipped() then text:SetText("--") frame.tooltip = nil return end local base, posBuff, negBuff = UnitRangedAttackPower(unit) PaperDollFormatStat(RANGED_ATTACK_POWER, base, posBuff, negBuff, frame, text) frame.tooltipSubtext = format(RANGED_ATTACK_POWER_TOOLTIP, math.max(base + posBuff + negBuff, 0) / ATTACK_POWER_MAGIC_NUMBER) end
-- ref PaperDollFormatStat (l.804-833). function PaperDollFormatStat(name, base, posBuff, negBuff, frame, textString) local effective = math.max(0, base + posBuff + negBuff) local text = HIGHLIGHT_FONT_COLOR_CODE .. name .. " " .. effective if posBuff == 0 and negBuff == 0 then text = text .. FONT_COLOR_CODE_CLOSE textString:SetText(effective) else if posBuff > 0 or negBuff < 0 then text = text .. " (" .. base .. FONT_COLOR_CODE_CLOSE end if posBuff > 0 then text = text .. FONT_COLOR_CODE_CLOSE .. GREEN_FONT_COLOR_CODE .. "+" .. posBuff .. FONT_COLOR_CODE_CLOSE end if negBuff < 0 then text = text .. RED_FONT_COLOR_CODE .. " " .. negBuff .. FONT_COLOR_CODE_CLOSE end if posBuff > 0 or negBuff < 0 then text = text .. HIGHLIGHT_FONT_COLOR_CODE .. ")" .. FONT_COLOR_CODE_CLOSE end if negBuff < 0 then textString:SetText(RED_FONT_COLOR_CODE .. effective .. FONT_COLOR_CODE_CLOSE) else textString:SetText(GREEN_FONT_COLOR_CODE .. effective .. FONT_COLOR_CODE_CLOSE) end end frame.tooltip = text end
-- ref PaperDollStatTooltip(unit, stat) (l.786-802), signature-exact: the button is the -- ambient `this` the reference reads, NOT a leading parameter, and `unit` leads `stat` -- exactly as the ref declares them (its pet rows pass "pet" — ref PetPaperDollFrame.xml:345; -- ours likewise, decision 1057). A leading frame parameter here was a wrong SHAPE behind a -- right name — 1199's failure mode — because an addon calls the 1.12 arity. function PaperDollStatTooltip(unit, stat) local button = this -- classFileName nil until the first player snapshot lands (this file's SetLevel comment -- on the same engine timing gap) — "" just misses every class lookup, falling through to -- DEFAULT_*_TOOLTIP below exactly like an unrecognized class would. A pet has no class -- either, so the pet rows land on the same DEFAULT_* fallback the ref gives them. local _, classFileName = UnitClass(unit or "player") classFileName = classFileName or "" local classStatText = getglobal(strupper(classFileName) .. "_" .. stat .. "_TOOLTIP") if not classStatText then classStatText = getglobal("DEFAULT_" .. stat .. "_TOOLTIP") end GameTooltip:SetOwner(button, "ANCHOR_RIGHT") GameTooltip:SetText(button.tooltip) GameTooltip:AddLine(classStatText, NORMAL_FONT_COLOR.r, NORMAL_FONT_COLOR.g, NORMAL_FONT_COLOR.b, 1) GameTooltip:Show() end

-- ── The 19 equipment slots + ammo (ref PaperDollItemSlotButton_*, l.78-98/594-784) ────── -- Cooldowns, the broken-red tint, and SHOW_COMPARE_TOOLTIP are still OMITTED this phase — -- this file's header comment. What ships now (1b): the icon/count fill, the empty-slot -- art, the hover tooltip, click-to-equip/-use (l.647-662, ctrl/shift named deferrals), -- the drag trio, lock dimming, and the CURSOR_UPDATE ring highlight (emulated — header -- comment). function BenillaPaperDollSlot_OnLoad(button, slotName) button:RegisterEvent("UNIT_INVENTORY_CHANGED") local id, texture, checkRelic = GetInventorySlotInfo(slotName) button.invSlotId = id button.slotName = slotName button.emptyTexture = texture button.checkRelic = checkRelic -- UnitHasRelicSlot is vanilla-always-false (header OMIT): never read button.icon = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "IconTexture") button.count = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Count") -- Equip interactions on the 19 named slots use the equip-swap wire (PickupInventoryItem -- pick/place/swap). The ammo slot (id 0) is different: it LOADS ammo by entry via -- CMSG_SET_AMMO (decision 0526; wow-re cursor-dragdrop-slots.md — the client's auto-equip -- sender forks ammo-class → SET_AMMO), so it only wants click-to-place + drag-drop, both -- routed to BenillaCharacterAmmoSlot_OnClick (its own Scripts block below). It carries no -- ring, so the CURSOR_UPDATE highlight / ITEM_LOCK dim legs would no-op anyway, and there -- is no drag-OUT (you can't pick the loaded ammo off the slot). if slotName ~= "AmmoSlot" then button:RegisterEvent("ITEM_LOCK_CHANGED") button:RegisterEvent("CURSOR_UPDATE") -- The shift-compare listener (ref PaperDollFrame.lua l.83): the ENGINE fires -- SHOW_COMPARE_TOOLTIP(slot, n) for an equippable item hover while shift is held; -- only the matching visible doll slot answers (the OnEvent branch below). button:RegisterEvent("SHOW_COMPARE_TOOLTIP") button:RegisterForClicks("LeftButtonUp", "RightButtonUp") -- The drag trio (decision 0216 §3): click-carry and drag are ONE code path in the -- reference (PaperDollFrame.xml:20-25 routes OnDragStart/OnReceiveDrag to the same -- OnClick("LeftButton", ignoreModifiers=1) the plain click uses) — see -- BenillaPaperDollSlot_OnClick below for the identical routing, the bag slots' own -- precedent (BagFrame.xml's BenillaBagSlot_OnClick). button:RegisterForDrag("LeftButton") else button:RegisterForClicks("LeftButtonUp") end BenillaPaperDollSlot_Update(button) end
-- Left: the reference's own modifier fork (ref l.647-660) — CTRL previews the worn -- item in the dressing room (decision 1060), SHIFT posts its link into an open chat edit -- box (decision 1059), and neither falls through to a pickup a real modified click would -- never trigger. Plain click: PickupInventoryItem (pick up / place / swap / cancel, -- ref l.656). Right: UseInventoryItem (ref l.659). `ignoreModifiers` is the drag-route -- calls' own suppression, the bag slots' precedent. function BenillaPaperDollSlot_OnClick(button, mouseButton, ignoreModifiers) if mouseButton == "LeftButton" then if IsControlKeyDown() and not ignoreModifiers then DressUpItemLink(GetInventoryItemLink("player", button.invSlotId)) return elseif IsShiftKeyDown() and not ignoreModifiers then -- Both of the ref's guards (l.652: only when the edit box is up) plus our own -- nil-link one live in the shared helper (UIParent.xml). A shift-click with chat -- closed does nothing here — a worn item has no stack to split, unlike a bag slot. BenillaChatEdit_InsertLink(GetInventoryItemLink("player", button.invSlotId)) return end PickupInventoryItem(button.invSlotId) GameTooltip:Hide() -- the item just left the slot for the cursor BenillaPaperDollSlot_Update(button) elseif mouseButton == "RightButton" then UseInventoryItem(button.invSlotId) end end
-- The ammo slot's own click/drop (decision 0526): ammo LOADS by entry (CMSG_SET_AMMO), it -- doesn't swap into an equip slot, so it can't share BenillaPaperDollSlot_OnClick's -- PickupInventoryItem path. Only an ammo payload fits (CursorCanGoInSlot(0) — ammo's -- find_equip_slot is [0]); the drop funnels through AutoEquipCursorItem, whose app-side drain -- resolves the held item's entry and forks to SET_AMMO — the reference's own shared auto-equip -- sender (wow-re cursor-dragdrop-slots.md). An empty cursor or a non-ammo payload is inert -- (nothing fits), and there is no unload-via-slot in 1.12. function BenillaCharacterAmmoSlot_OnClick(button) if CursorCanGoInSlot(button.invSlotId) then AutoEquipCursorItem() GameTooltip:Hide() BenillaPaperDollSlot_Update(button) end end
function BenillaPaperDollSlot_Update(button) local textureName = GetInventoryItemTexture("player", button.invSlotId) if textureName then button.icon:SetTexture(textureName) local count = GetInventoryItemCount("player", button.invSlotId) if (count or 0) > 1 then button.count:SetText(count) else button.count:SetText("") end else button.icon:SetTexture(button.emptyTexture) button.count:SetText("") end -- A BROKEN item (durability 0) tints icon + slot ring red — ref -- PaperDollItemSlotButton_Update (l.670-676: SetItemButtonTextureVertexColor + -- SetItemButtonNormalTextureVertexColor, both 0.9, 0, 0). The bags carry no broken -- tint in 1.12 (ContainerFrame.lua has none) — equipped only. Kept as a flag for -- the cursor highlight's restore (Unlock below shares the ring). button.broken = textureName and GetInventoryItemBroken("player", button.invSlotId) -- A locked slot (its item is up on the cursor, or a send is still pending -- server-side, decision 0216 §4/0218 §3) dims — the bag slots' own vertex-dim -- convention (BagFrame.xml's BenillaBagSlot_Update), applied here instead of the -- ref's separate SetItemButtonDesaturated call (no engine equivalent — header -- comment). The transient drag-dim outranks the broken red on the icon. if IsInventoryItemLocked(button.invSlotId) then button.icon:SetVertexColor(0.4, 0.4, 0.4) elseif button.broken then button.icon:SetVertexColor(0.9, 0, 0) else button.icon:SetVertexColor(1, 1, 1) end BenillaPaperDollSlot_UnlockHighlight(button) if GameTooltip:IsOwned(button) then BenillaPaperDollSlot_OnEnter(button) end end
-- ref PaperDollItemSlotButton_OnEnter (l.739-748): the equipped hover is the INSTANCE -- render — SetInventoryItem, never an id/template render. That carries the live -- durability pair (an earlier SetItemById here read the template's full max/max), and -- an instance hover never arms a shift-compare — the engine's SetInventoryItem doesn't -- arm (a worn item compared with itself is no comparison; director-caught: shift over -- the doll popped a "Currently Equipped" 0/XX beside a template-full main tooltip). -- The ref's repair-mode branch (l.757-762) is INTERIM-omitted with the binding's -- repairCost. checkRelic (l.744-746) is TBC-flagged dead weight in 1.12 — omitted. function BenillaPaperDollSlot_OnEnter(button) GameTooltip:SetOwner(button, "ANCHOR_RIGHT") local hasItem = GameTooltip:SetInventoryItem("player", button.invSlotId) if not hasItem then -- Empty slot: the slot-name tooltip (ref strupper(strsub(name,10)) -> the matching -- GlobalStrings key, e.g. "HeadSlot" -> HEADSLOT -> "Head"). GameTooltip:SetText(getglobal(strupper(button.slotName)) or button.slotName) end GameTooltip:Show() end
-- CURSOR_UPDATE's LockHighlight/UnlockHighlight emulation (this file's header comment: no -- true forced-highlight affordance exists — no benilla-ui Button method shows a state -- texture off real hover). A vertex tint on the slot's own Quickslot2 ring -- (`NormalTexture`, the template below) stands in: green while `CursorCanGoInSlot` says -- the held payload fits here, white otherwise. -- Both legs no-op on a ringless slot (the ammo slot carries no NormalTexture). function BenillaPaperDollSlot_LockHighlight(button) local ring = button:GetNormalTexture() if ring then ring:SetVertexColor(0, 1, 0) end end
-- The restore leg: back to the ring's resting color — broken red (ref l.672) or white. function BenillaPaperDollSlot_UnlockHighlight(button) local ring = button:GetNormalTexture() if not ring then return end if button.broken then ring:SetVertexColor(0.9, 0, 0) else ring:SetVertexColor(1, 1, 1) end end
function BenillaPaperDollSlot_OnEvent(button) if event == "UNIT_INVENTORY_CHANGED" and arg1 == "player" then BenillaPaperDollSlot_Update(button) elseif event == "ITEM_LOCK_CHANGED" then -- Ref PaperDollItemSlotButton_OnEvent (l.601-604): no arg filtering — every doll -- slot just repaints on any lock transition (cheap, idempotent; it's this SLOT's -- own dim that's actually changing, if anything is). BenillaPaperDollSlot_Update(button) elseif event == "CURSOR_UPDATE" then if CursorCanGoInSlot(button.invSlotId) then BenillaPaperDollSlot_LockHighlight(button) else BenillaPaperDollSlot_UnlockHighlight(button) end elseif event == "SHOW_COMPARE_TOOLTIP" then -- ref PaperDollItemSlotButton_OnEvent (l.621-640, quoted; button.invSlotId for the -- ref's this:GetID()): arg1 = the doll slot the hovered item would equip into, -- arg2 = which shopping tooltip. Both anchor to THIS doll slot (1 to its right, -- 2 hanging below-right) — so compares appear only with the character window -- open, the 1.12 behavior. if arg1 ~= button.invSlotId or not button:IsVisible() or arg2 > NUM_SHOPPING_TOOLTIPS then return end local tooltip = getglobal("ShoppingTooltip" .. arg2) local anchor = "ANCHOR_RIGHT" if arg2 > 1 then anchor = "ANCHOR_BOTTOMRIGHT" end tooltip:SetOwner(button, anchor) local hasItem = tooltip:SetInventoryItem("player", button.invSlotId) if not hasItem then tooltip:Hide() end end end
-- ref PaperDollItemSlotButton_OnUpdate (l.766-784), the un-throttled BagFrame-style -- re-enter loop (BagFrame.xml's own comment on why this ships unthrottled). function BenillaPaperDollSlot_OnUpdate(button) if GameTooltip:IsOwned(button) then BenillaPaperDollSlot_OnEnter(button) end end
-- ── The model pane (ref UIParent.lua:1420-1462) ───────────────────────────────────────── -- This file's header comment: a booth-texture stand-in, not a live widget. `frame` here is -- CharacterModelFrame; `frame.facing` stands in for the ref's `model.rotation`. -- These four are the ref's SHARED Model_* helpers (UIParent.lua), and they are shared here -- too: the pet page's pane (decision 1057) drives the very same code. The one thing that -- differs per pane is WHERE the yaw goes — the engine has no `Model:SetFacing` widget -- method, so each pane has its own booth-yaw binding — so the pane names its own in -- `frame.setFacing` at OnLoad and these read it. (The inspect window still carries its own -- copy of this quartet, predating the generalization; folding it in is a follow-up, not -- this slice's to churn.) function BenillaPaperDollModel_OnLoad(frame) frame.facing = 0.61 -- ref UIParent.lua:1422, the literal default facing frame.setFacing(frame.facing) end
-- ref Model_RotateLeft/Right (UIParent.lua:1426-1442) — the ref's OWN left/right sign -- convention is preserved verbatim (rotate-left SUBTRACTS, rotate-right ADDS); not -- re-derived, just quoted. function BenillaPaperDollModel_RotateLeft(frame) frame.facing = frame.facing - 0.03 frame.setFacing(frame.facing) PlaySound("igInventoryRotateCharacter") end
function BenillaPaperDollModel_RotateRight(frame) frame.facing = frame.facing + 0.03 frame.setFacing(frame.facing) PlaySound("igInventoryRotateCharacter") end
-- ref Model_OnUpdate (UIParent.lua:1444-1462) — the HELD-button continuous spin, which is -- where a rotate button's actual feel lives: half a turn per second (ROTATIONS_PER_SECOND, -- UIParent.lua:2), against which the 0.03 click nudge above is a ~1.7° tap. Every 1.12 model -- pane wires it (PaperDollFrame l.222-224, DressUpFrame.xml:202-204, TabardFrame.xml:406-408). -- It used to be omitted here for want of `GetButtonState` — that method now answers "PUSHED" -- for a LIVE mouse-held button (decision 0288 P3), so the ref's own loop ships here. -- That INCLUDES the ref's sign quirk: the held branches run OPPOSITE to the click helpers -- (held-LEFT adds, held-RIGHT subtracts). Not a slip of ours — the ref's own, not re-derived. function BenillaPaperDollModel_OnUpdate(frame, elapsed) local step = elapsed * 2 * PI * ROTATIONS_PER_SECOND if getglobal(frame:GetName() .. "RotateLeftButton"):GetButtonState() == "PUSHED" then frame.facing = frame.facing + step if frame.facing < 0 then frame.facing = frame.facing + (2 * PI) end frame.setFacing(frame.facing) end if getglobal(frame:GetName() .. "RotateRightButton"):GetButtonState() == "PUSHED" then frame.facing = frame.facing - step if frame.facing > (2 * PI) then frame.facing = frame.facing - (2 * PI) end frame.setFacing(frame.facing) end end
-- ref CharacterModelFrame_OnMouseUp (l.31-35): a plain left-click-up on the model pane -- also auto-equips a held container item — the model pane doubles as a drop target even -- without a drag, not just via OnReceiveDrag. AutoEquipCursorItem is already a no-op for -- every non-fitting/non-container payload (cursor.rs's own contract), so no CursorHasItem -- guard is needed here. function BenillaPaperDollModel_OnMouseUp(frame, button) if button == "LeftButton" then AutoEquipCursorItem() end end
